newsitem.title: UK: BP says sees slower eps, div growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: BP says sees slower eps, div growth in 1997.

text.p: British Petroleum Plc said on Tuesday it expected dividend and earnings per share growth to be at a lower rate in the current year than the 30 percent posted in 1996.
"It is hard to sustain 30 percent growth," chairman David Simon told reporters at the company's annual results press conference.
Simon called such a growth rate "unrealistic", although he added that the current business environment looked good.
"The industrial climate is promising, we cannot ask for more," he said.
BP earlier reported a big jump in its net replacement cost profit for calendar 1996 which climbed by nearly a third to a record 2.62 billion stg.

"We have sown the seeds for some good years to come," chief executive John Browne said, adding that two-thirds of the profit increase was due to BP's own efforts, including boosting production and reducing costs.
Higher oil prices were the main outside factor helping profit growth.
